name: Select
summary: Lets people choose one option from a list that opens on demand.
description: A select shows the current choice in a closed box and opens a list of options when activated; the browser or the platform renders the list, its keyboard interaction and its announcements. It fits a choice among many known values (a country, a time zone, a sort order) where showing every option at once would take too much room. Two to about six options worth reading side by side are a Radio group; a list of actions is a Dropdown.

anatomy.description: Root. Stacks the label, the control, the description and the error message; carries the size and the forced state.
Text naming the field. Provides the accessible name; activating it focuses the control.
Box holding the control and the chevron drawn over its end edge.
The native select, drawn by the component as a closed box showing the chosen option. Receives focus, holds the value; the browser opens and renders the list.
Chevron glyph of the icon font at the end edge of the control, saying that it opens a list. Hidden from assistive technology, which learns it from the role.
One choice in the list, rendered by the browser: the component gives it no style of its own.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: Text of the option, what people read and what is announced.

properties.name: Value
properties.description: Value submitted when the option is chosen. Defaults to the option's position.

properties.name: Selected
properties.description: Whether this option is the current choice.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: The option stays in the list, dimmed, and cannot be chosen.

anatomy.description: Optional help text under the control (format, example, consequence), associated with it as its description.
Text describing the error when the field is invalid, associated with the control as a description. Shown only while invalid.

properties.name: Size
properties.description: Control height, inline padding and text size scale together; label, description and error keep their size.

options.description: Dense forms, toolbars, table rows (32 px high).
Prominent, single fields: a search page, a sign-in form (48 px).

properties.name: Label
properties.description: What the field asks for, as a noun phrase (Email address). Always visible.

properties.name: Placeholder
properties.description: Text shown while no option is chosen (Choose a country). A disabled, unselectable first option: never the label.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Help text: expected format, example, or what the value is used for.

properties.name: Error message
properties.description: What is wrong and how to fix it, shown when the field is invalid.

properties.name: Required
properties.description: The field must be filled to submit the form.

properties.name: Invalid
properties.description: The value failed validation: the border takes the error color and the error message is shown.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Non-interactive and skipped by the keyboard; the value stays visible. Prefer read-only when people may need to read or copy the value.

states.description: Resting: an outlined box on the default surface.
Pointer over the control. The box takes the surface hover tint; the border does not change. Needs a pointing device: touch has no hover.
Keyboard focus on the control. Shows the shared focus ring outside its border; pointer focus shows none.
Validation failed: the border takes the error color and the error message is shown under the control.
Non-interactive. Box, value, label and description drop to the shared disabled colors; hover and focus do not apply.

notes: Label, control, description and error message stack, separated by container.gap; the control fills the width of the component, which the layout sizes.
Inline padding, minimum height and text size come from the size option; the corner radius and the border width do not change.
The chevron sits over the end edge of the control, which reserves room for it with padding-inline-end.

name.text: Computed from the label, associated with the control as its label element on the web. The description and the error message are exposed as the accessible description, not as part of the name.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to the control. A disabled control is not focusable and is skipped.
Open the list and move through the options the way the platform's native select does; the browser owns this interaction.

guidelines.text: Expose the combobox role, the name, the value and the required, disabled and invalid states through the platform's native select, so assistive technology receives them without extra work.

Use the native select element rendered as a drop-down box: it exposes the combobox role, its value and states, and the browser owns the list, its keyboard interaction and its announcements. The list is not styled by the component.
Every field has a visible label associated with the control programmatically; help text that people need to fill the field (format, example) is visible too, as the description.
Associate the label with a label element whose for attribute names the control's id; reference the description and the error message with aria-describedby, so they are read after the name.
Use a pop-up button to present a flat list of mutually exclusive options or states.
The chevron is decorative and hidden from assistive technology with aria-hidden="true": an icon-font glyph is written as its ligature name, which would otherwise be read with the value.
When the value is invalid, identify the field and describe the error in text next to it: the error message names what is wrong and how to fix it, and is associated with the control.
Say that the value is invalid with aria-invalid on the control, and that a field is required with the required attribute, which the browser exposes as required.
Mark required fields in the label or the description, never by the error color alone.

Label, value, description and error text contrast at least 4.5:1 with their background in every color mode and enabled state: label and value 19.07:1 (light) and 11.27:1 (dark) on the default surface, description 12.87:1 and 8.80:1, placeholder 6.08:1 and 6.36:1, error text 4.52:1 and 4.97:1 (4.26:1 on a level 1 surface in light mode, a Figma library limit tracked as a known issue). Disabled text is inactive and exempt.

The border is what identifies the field, so it contrasts at least 3:1 with the adjacent surface in every color mode: 12.87:1 (light) and 8.80:1 (dark) on the default surface at rest, 12.14:1 and 8.06:1 on the hover tint; the error border 6.12:1 and 3.82:1; the focus ring 5.79:1 and 12.80:1. Disabled is exempt.
A visible focus indicator appears when the control receives focus, drawn outside its border.
The focus ring is drawn with :focus-visible, so pointer focus on the closed control shows no ring.
Every size is a pointer target of at least 24 x 24 CSS pixels through its minimum height: 32, 40 and 48 pixels.
A disabled select leaves the focus order; a disabled option stays in the list, announced as dimmed, and cannot be chosen.
Apple recommends a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt; the small and medium sizes (32 and 40 pt) fall under it on iOS today: the Figma library has no platform heights.

Android recommends a touch target of at least 48 x 48 dp; the small and medium sizes (32 and 40 dp) fall under it on Android today. Expose an invalid value with the error semantics so the message is announced with the field.
Color transitions of the control are removed when the user asks for reduced motion.

guidelines: The label is a noun phrase naming the choice: Country, Time zone, Sort by. Sentence case, no colon, no trailing punctuation.
Option labels are short and parallel; order them logically (alphabetical for long lists, most common first for short ones).
The placeholder, when any, is an invitation to choose (Choose a country), shown until a choice is made; it is never a valid value.
The error message says what to do: Choose a country.

examples.name: Medium, with a choice and a description
Medium, required and invalid
examples.description: No choice made in a required field; the error message says what to do.

decisions.text: The control is a box on the default surface outlined in the accent neutral border color; hover tints it with the surface hover color and keeps the border; invalid takes the base error border; disabled takes the shared disabled colors. Value text is primary, the placeholder tertiary, the description secondary, the error message the error text color.
decisions.rationale: The Figma library maps no color to form controls. The accent neutral border is the lightest neutral border that keeps 3:1 against the surface in both modes (WCAG 1.4.11); the hover tint reuses the surface's own hover step.

decisions.text: Three sizes from the Figma library's space and body scales: small (32 px high, 8 px inline padding, 14 px text), medium (40, 12, 16, the default) and large (48, 16, 20); the border is 0.6 px (stroke-width.sm) and the corners 4 px (corner-radius.xs) at every size; label, description and error message keep 14 px.

A field always has a visible label above the control; help text goes under the control as the description, and the error message under it while the field is invalid. Both are exposed as the control's description.

The select is the platform's native select: the component styles the closed box and its chevron only; the opened list, its keyboard interaction and its announcements belong to the browser or the platform and are not specified here.
decisions.rationale: A custom list needs script to be accessible (focus management, arrow keys, type-ahead), and the web implementation ships none.

decisions.text: A chevron (expand_more, the icon font) sits over the end edge of the control at 16, 20 or 24 px by size, 8 px from the edge; the control reserves 28, 36 or 40 px of end padding for it. It follows the value color and is hidden from assistive technology.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions field-colors, sizes, label-description-error, native-list, chevron-indicator). Native select in a wrapper with a label element, a chevron, a description and an error message; options as a repeated part; states default, hover, focus-visible, invalid, disabled; sizes small, medium, large. Contrast on the default surface, light / dark: label and value 19.07 / 11.27, description 12.87 / 8.80, error text 4.52 / 4.97 (4.26 on level 1 in light mode), border at rest 12.87 / 8.80 and 12.14 / 8.06 on hover, error border 6.12 / 3.82, focus ring 5.79 / 12.80.
